propositions: A rejected tickets-branch auto-push fails silently: the writer receives success while the push is rejected by GitHub push protection, leaving commits diverged locally and undetectable to other agents.
The rejection reason (e.g., GH013 secret-scan block) is captured by git but discarded before reaching the caller, visible only via manual git push.
The divergence backlog is not re-announced on subsequent writes, allowing eight-hour-long accumulation of unpushed commits to go unnoticed.
Ticket event payloads (comments with raw environment output) are never scanned for secrets on write, only code passes the gitleaks gate.
The over-broad `rejected` substring classifier misroutes policy-decline rejections onto the retry path, causing three futile fetch+merge cycles instead of immediate terminal reporting.
